description: Explain the architecture by which background jobs are defined, enqueued and executed in the Twenty server. In particular: how does a class become a job handler, how does a job name map to a handler method when several handler classes share a queue, how are workers started and filtered per deployment, how do per-queue concurrency/lock settings reach the underlying queue library, and how is a request-scoped handler instantiated with the workspace context?
anchor_note: non-bug task: root_cause_symbols holds the anchor (entry point / changed symbol); RC metrics are reported for category A only
alternatives: Drivers other than BullMQ exist (drivers/sync.driver.ts, drivers/memory) selected by module factory; same explorer works over the driver abstraction.
Cron jobs are registered with addCron (message-queue.service.ts ~line 82) and still dispatch by job name through the same explorer.

source.verification: Read cited lines; confirm Process/Processor metadata via message-queue-metadata.accessor.ts.
source.notes: Key insight an agent must find: all processor classes on a queue share ONE worker callback and each job is offered to every group; routing is by job.name vs @Process argument (handleProcessor filtering). Confounders: queue name vs job name; job name is conventionally Class.name.

evidence: packages/twenty-server/src/engine/core-modules/message-queue/__tests__/message-queue.explorer.spec.ts:29 'lets a decorated processor publish progress through its context'

notes: architecture claims verified in message-queue.explorer.ts: explore() discovers @Processor providers, groups by queue (groupProcessorsByQueueName), filters with WORKER_ENABLED_QUEUES/WORKER_EXCLUDED_QUEUES via shouldCreateWorkerForQueue, passes MESSAGE_QUEUE_WORKER_CONFIG[queue].workerOptions; handleProcessorGroupCollection registers one queue.work callback per queue and offers each job to every processor group; handleProcessor filters methods by job.name === @Process jobName; request-scoped providers use createContextId + registerRequestByContextId + injector.loadPerContext

mapping note gt_path[7] / relevant[3] MESSAGE_QUEUE_WORKER_CONFIG entry at :151 is the workspaceDestroyQueue example: key is the const MESSAGE_QUEUE_WORKER_CONFIG (ok); the gt is conceptual (not a call chain) so path order is not significant

missing keys: shouldCreateWorkerForQueue (utils/should-create-worker-for-queue.util.ts), MessageQueueExplorer.groupProcessorsByQueueName, MessageQueueExplorer.invokeProcessMethods, MessageQueueService.work (message-queue.service.ts:116, bridges to the driver); BullMQDriver.work is the options->Worker mapping

distractors: MessageQueueWorkerDrainService and FairQueueScheduler exist (fairness/ is a directory; FairQueueScheduler is even used in BullMQDriver.work:364 -> not a clean distractor, drop); src/engine/core-modules/cron holds only CronModule and sentry-cron-monitor decorator (claim "schedules cron registrations" false) -> drop
